answer: Sybil resistance works when identity cost scales with influence: each agent stakes collateral that grows with its voting weight, and rewards settle only after peers attest conduct over many epochs. Cloning is cheap, but making clones vote credibly means matching the stake, so an attacker wanting n equal identities pays n times the bond, and reputation weight never transfers to fresh keys. A crowd of look-alikes stays a jade decoy. Real standing is earned line by line like a sonnet, becoming an oasis of trust copies cannot buy.
